summary: Mason County, WA state lookout: a 1944 Aircraft Warning cabin, then a 40-foot DNR tower from 1964 removed in 1969; no standing structure described today.

facts.design: Aircraft Warning Service crew station with an observation room, replaced in 1964 by a 40-foot timber live-in DNR tower
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1969; sources describe only concrete fragments on the summit

access.note: Willhite Web says permits are now required on most roads to the top; an old trail is an alternative

visit.trail_note: Any vehicle can reach the gate where the trail starts; the route described is 3 miles one way on foot

events.note: Aircraft Warning Service building moved from Lost Lake Hills to Dayton Peak
10 by 10 observation room built on top (Willhite Web account)
Gerald and Stephie Needham move in with four children, per Needham's account

Public power connected; described as first Division of Forestry lookout with public power
Cabin replaced by a 40-foot timber live-in DNR tower, a quarter mile (or half mile) southeast of the first site
Curtis Snow official lookout (timeline says Kurt Snow); David Wood on relief
Tower removed; register and firelookout.com describe the removal as abrupt

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register point N 47 11.686 W 123 13.880 matches the brief's FFLOS coordinates and is kept. The brief's second point (47.1891, -123.2239) was not checked. Willhite Web places the first lookout on the northwest peak and assumes the 1964 tower stood on the highest summit.

The 1944 move of the Aircraft Warning building is consistent across sources. The register dates the first lookout to 1946; Willhite Web gives a 10 by 10 room in summer 1945; the Forest Lookouts page quotes an annual report saying a 10 by 10 tower was added in 1946. Not resolved; the story gives both.
Three miles (Willhite Web intro), six miles (firelookout.com) and eight miles (a newspaper visit quoted by Willhite Web). Not resolved; the story gives all three.
The register gives 20 by 40 feet; Willhite Web gives 14 by 32 feet. Not resolved.
Quarter mile southeast (Willhite Web, Forest Lookouts) against half mile southeast (firelookout.com). Not resolved; the story gives both.

889 feet (firelookout.com; the brief's 271 m matches this), 1,250 feet at the tower as quoted by Willhite Web, and summit elevations of 1,013 and 1,066 feet. Brief figure kept; elevation is not in the story.
The same Willhite Web page calls him Kurt Snow in the year-by-year timeline and Curtis Snow in the 1965 article. The story uses Curtis Snow and notes the timeline spelling.
Needham's own account gives May 1945 as the move-in date, while a 1963 line says they had been there since 1944, with the writer's doubt noted. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Staffing as_of is the last year named in our reading (1966). The 1944-1969 history rests mostly on Willhite Web; the register and firelookout.com supply the 1946 date, the 1964 replacement and the abrupt 1969 removal. Access level 'permission' is inferred from Willhite Web's note on permits, not an agency statement. No photos added (licences not checked). Distance, cabin size, replacement location and elevation disagree across sources and are reported as such.
